# @verevoir/llm

Provider-agnostic LLM call surface with token + cost accounting.

## Purpose

Lets a downstream project make LLM calls with retry-friendly errors, token
accounting, per-direction cost tracking, and tool-calling, without coupling to a
specific provider SDK. Pick the provider you use via a subpath import; the unused
SDK does not enter your bundle.

## Subpaths

- `@verevoir/llm` — core types, the `chat()` / tool-calling contracts, cost
  accounting, and the model catalog + provider-routing helpers. No SDK dependency.
- `@verevoir/llm/anthropic` — Anthropic SDK adapter (`chat`, `chatWithTools`,
  `chatWithToolLoop`, live `onProgress`). Requires `@anthropic-ai/sdk`.
- `@verevoir/llm/vertex` — Claude on Google Cloud Vertex AI: the Anthropic
  adapter with a different client (`chat`, `chatWithTools`, `chatWithToolLoop`,
  `PROVIDER`, namespaced `vertex`). Requires `@anthropic-ai/vertex-sdk`, an
  optional peer that only this subpath imports; that package declares
  `@anthropic-ai/sdk` as its own dependency, so it is not installed separately,
  and this subpath does not load the direct route's client module. The
  requests, the cache breakpoints for each `cache` value, the tool loop, the
  retries and the usage figures (cache writes and reads and the five-minute /
  one-hour split included) are the Anthropic adapter's own, from one shared
  implementation.
  Authentication is Google Cloud's standard credentials flow, run by the Vertex
  SDK; there is no API key (a per-call `apiKey` is refused, and
  `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` / `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` are never read). The project
  and region come from `ANTHROPIC_VERTEX_PROJECT_ID` and `CLOUD_ML_REGION`
  (`ChatOptions` has no field for them); a missing one is refused before any
  call with a plain error naming the variable. The model name is sent exactly
  as given — `model` when set, else the Anthropic catalogue's id for the
  `modelClass` — with no mapping: where Vertex AI names a model differently,
  pass that name as `model`. `TokenUsage.provider` is `'vertex'` and `route` is
  `'google-cloud'`; the price book has no entry of its own for that provider,
  so a call is priced only if the exact model name sent (or `vertex/<model>`)
  has an entry, else `unpriced` — pricing Vertex calls is the caller's concern.
  `classifyLlmError` gives the same kinds as on the direct route (the Vertex
  SDK throws the Anthropic SDK's own error classes). Registers nothing into the
  model catalogue or the connection registry, so routing does not know it.
- `@verevoir/llm/google` — Google Gemini SDK adapter (`chat`, `chatWithTools`,
  `chatWithToolLoop` as of 0.13.0). Requires `@google/genai`.
- `@verevoir/llm/openai` — OpenAI adapter via the Responses API
  (`chat`; `chatWithTools` + `chatWithToolLoop` via the OpenAI-compatible factory).
  Requires `openai`. The only keyless-capable adapter: a base-URL override with a
  blank key points it at a local server (LM Studio / Ollama / vLLM).
- `@verevoir/llm/deepseek` — DeepSeek adapter, OpenAI-compatible via the Chat
  Completions API at `https://api.deepseek.com`. Reuses the `openai` peer — no
  separate SDK. `chat` + tool-calling.
- `@verevoir/llm/samba` — SambaNova adapter (`SAMBA_NOVA_API_KEY`),
  OpenAI-compatible. `chat` + tool-calling.
- `@verevoir/llm/mistral` — Mistral adapter (`MISTRAL_API_KEY`),
  OpenAI-compatible. `chat` + tool-calling.
- `@verevoir/llm/claude-cli` — shells out to the real Claude Code CLI
  (`claude -p`) as a subscription-only substrate, for a caller that must run on
  a subscription credential rather than a billed API key (imitating Claude Code
  to the raw Messages API is not a sanctioned route). Provider id `'claude-cli'`,
  deliberately distinct from `'anthropic'`; never registered into the model
  catalog or connection registry — `resolveModel`/`resolveModelByTerm` can never
  silently substitute it, a caller wanting this substrate imports and calls it
  directly. `chat()` only. No SDK dependency — it spawns a subprocess, and
  that subprocess's environment is built from an allowlist — only `PATH`,
  `HOME`, `TMPDIR`, and the CLI's own subscription-credential env var
  (`CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`) and `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` (a path; see the CHANGELOG
  SECURITY entry for 0.36.0) ever reach it; nothing else in the caller's
  environment is passed through (but see that entry: a stored metered
  login is still reachable). Replaced an
  earlier denylist that had already missed one live credential vector
  (`ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN`) in an earlier version — a denylist can only
  exclude names someone thought of; the allowlist doesn't need to.
  Fresh-spawn `chat()` calls are bounded by an IDLE-output timeout (not
  wall-clock — resets on every stdout/stderr chunk, including tool-call
  activity, so tool time never counts as silence): default 10 minutes,
  override per call via `idleTimeoutMs` or process-wide via
  `CLAUDE_CLI_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS`. On expiry the child is killed and the call
  rejects with `.code === 'CLAUDE_CLI_IDLE_TIMEOUT'` plus `.timeoutMs`.

Every provider in the matrix (Anthropic, Google, OpenAI, DeepSeek, SambaNova,
Mistral) can now drive the tool loop. `claude-cli` is a separate, deliberately
non-interchangeable substrate and is not part of that matrix.

- `@verevoir/llm/catalog` — registers every catalogued provider's model
  catalogue (anthropic, mistral, samba) AND connection (env var names only) as
  an import side effect, with **no SDK import anywhere in its import graph** —
  unlike the real adapter subpaths above, each of which requires its SDK as a
  peer dependency. For a consumer that only needs `resolveModelByTerm`, a
  label, or a rate (never a real call) — e.g. selecting a reviewer model by
  name — importing this subpath resolves it with zero SDK as a transitive
  dependency. Also re-exports the raw `ANTHROPIC_CATALOG` / `MISTRAL_CATALOG` /
  `SAMBA_CATALOG` arrays for a consumer that wants the data directly. The real
  adapter subpaths are unchanged for an existing consumer — each still
  registers its own catalogue + connection itself, idempotently, so importing
  both this subpath and a real adapter is a no-op the second time, not a
  conflict. `/openai`, `/deepseek`, `/google` are not included — they never
  used `ModelCatalogEntry`/`registerModelCatalog` in the first place. `/claude-cli`
  stays deliberately unregistered, per its own design.

## Install

```bash
npm install @verevoir/llm @anthropic-ai/sdk
```

The package's `peerDependencies` are marked optional — install only the SDK(s)
you import (`@anthropic-ai/sdk`, `@anthropic-ai/vertex-sdk`, `@google/genai`,
`openai`; the OpenAI-compatible providers share `openai`).

## Canonical usage

```ts
import { anthropic } from '@verevoir/llm/anthropic';

const reply = await anthropic.chat({
  systemPrompt: '...',
  turns: [{ role: 'user', content: '...' }],
  // Omit apiKey when auth is ambient: it resolves from the env
  // (CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN preferred, else ANTHROPIC_API_KEY). Pass apiKey
  // ONLY to force a specific key (BYOK) — an explicit key short-circuits OAuth.
  modelClass: 'reasoning', // 'reasoning' | 'drafting' | 'extraction'
});

// reply.content: string
// reply.usage:   { provider, model, direction, inputTokens, outputTokens, ... }
```

`ChatOptions.model` is an optional exact model id. When set it is the id sent,
exactly as given (no catalogue lookup, so a family name or alias is not
resolved); when not set the adapter sends `models[modelClass]`. Acted on by
`/anthropic`, `/vertex`, `/samba` and `/mistral` on `chat`, `chatWithTools` and
every call `chatWithToolLoop` makes, and by `/deepseek` on `chat`;
`/claude-cli` hands it to the CLI as `--model`; `/openai` and `/google` accept
and ignore it. `usage.model` and the
model span report the id sent; `usage.direction` stays the `modelClass` asked
for (`'reasoning'` when none was given).

## Tool calling

Each adapter exposes, alongside `chat()`:
- `chatWithTools(options)` — single-shot; surfaces the model's `ToolUse[]` for
  the caller to execute.
- `chatWithToolLoop(options)` — runs model → execute tools → feed results back →
  repeat, to a `maxIterations` cap. Takes a `ToolExecutor`
  (`(toolUse) => Promise<string | ContentBlock[]>`) plus per-iteration
  `onUsage` / `onIteration` hooks; usage is summed across the loop.

Provider-agnostic types `ToolDef`, `ToolUse`, `ToolExecutor`, `ContentBlock`
(`text` | `tool_use` | `tool_result` | `image` | `document`), plus
`UnsupportedContentBlockError` and `collapseContentToText(provider, content)`:
a provider that cannot carry a block type (only `@verevoir/llm/anthropic` and
`@verevoir/llm/vertex` carry `image`/`document`) throws this error, naming the provider and
block type. Inside a tool executor's result it becomes a named `is_error`
tool_result; inside a user turn the caller built, it throws. The
`ChatWithTools*` / `ChatWithToolLoop*` option/result shapes live on the
core export.

## Failures

A failed call rejects with what it always rejected with — the provider SDK's
own error, or this library's own plain `Error` — unwrapped. To classify one,
pass the caught error to `classifyLlmError(err)` (core export). It only reads
the error and returns a plain `LlmFailure` object:

- `kind: LlmErrorKind` — a closed union: `'authentication'` | `'permission'` |
  `'rate-limited'` | `'overloaded'` | `'unavailable'` | `'invalid-request'` |
  `'timeout'` | `'empty-response'` | `'other'`.
- `retryable: boolean` — whether a later attempt may succeed. True for
  `rate-limited`, `overloaded`, `unavailable`, `timeout`; false for the rest.

How a kind is recognised, first match wins: an `EmptyResponseError`
(`empty-response`); a `code` of `CLAUDE_CLI_IDLE_TIMEOUT` or
`CLAUDE_CLI_SESSION_TURN_TIMEOUT` (`timeout`); a numeric `status` — 401 `authentication`, 403
`permission`, 408 `timeout`, 429 `rate-limited`, 529 `overloaded`, any other 4xx
`invalid-request`, any other 5xx `unavailable`; a non-numeric status is never
coerced. Then, with no usable status, a string `type` — `overloaded_error`,
`rate_limit_error`, `api_error` (`unavailable`), `timeout_error` (what the
Anthropic SDK gives an error arriving mid-stream). Then the class name —
`APIConnectionTimeoutError` (`timeout`), `APIConnectionError` (`unavailable`).
Otherwise `other`. Message text is never read. `claude-cli` errors classify
only as `timeout` (its idle and turn timeouts) or `other` (it reports every
other failure as free text). An aborted `abortSignal`'s `reason` and the
library's own argument / configuration checks (no turns, no tools, a missing
API key, `UnsupportedContentBlockError`) are `other`; there is no `aborted`
kind.

Thrown errors are unchanged apart from two additions. `EmptyResponseError`
(core export, `extends Error`) is what every adapter's `chat()` throws when
the reply has no text, where it threw a plain `Error`: its `message` is
unchanged (`<provider>.chat: response had no text content (…)`) and its `name`
is still `Error`. The `claude-cli` held-session turn timeout now carries
`.code === 'CLAUDE_CLI_SESSION_TURN_TIMEOUT'`
(`CLAUDE_CLI_SESSION_TURN_TIMEOUT_CODE` on `@verevoir/llm/claude-cli`).

## Cost accounting

Every call returns a `TokenUsage` typed
`{ provider, model, direction, route, inputTokens, outputTokens, ... }` (with
optional `substrateVersion` — which version of an external substrate, e.g. the
`claude` CLI, served the call, `undefined` for a direct API adapter — and
optional `cacheRead` / `cacheWrite` so prompt-cache savings price at their own
rates). `route` (`CredentialRoute`, a core export: `'api-key'` |
`'subscription-oauth'` | `'google-cloud'` | `'mixed'`) reports which credential mechanism actually
served a call, positively, never left to be inferred from what's absent. The
core export ships `sumUsages` / `parseUsage` to roll up across calls,
`totalTokens`, `formatTokensCompact` for compact displays, and
`createPriceBook` / `book.costOf(...)` — the cost API, pricing from
LiteLLM's live price table (a bundled snapshot as fallback) and reporting an
unmatched model as `unpriced`, never `0`. The older `estimateCostUSD`,
`RatesTable` / `RateTuple`, `catalogEntryFor`, and `uncoveredModels` are kept
for back-compat but `@deprecated` — new code should use `createPriceBook`.

`ChatOptions.cache` (`'none' | 'default' | 'prefix'`) controls prompt
caching per call. Only `@verevoir/llm/anthropic` and `@verevoir/llm/vertex` act
on it (`chat`, `chatWithTools`, every `chatWithToolLoop` call); every other adapter accepts
and ignores it. `'default'` / omitted: the adapter's standard cache breakpoints
with the provider's five-minute lifetime. `'none'`: no `cache_control` anywhere
in the request — for a one-off call whose prefix nothing reads again, so it
pays no cache-write premium. `'prefix'`: one breakpoint on the system prompt
(tools + system prompt cache together) and never one on the conversation — for
a call that shares its system prompt with sibling calls but whose own
conversation nothing else reads. Within one tool loop `'prefix'` re-sends the
conversation uncached on every iteration: more plain input tokens per
iteration, no cache-write premium on the conversation; it pays only when the
conversation is short or nothing reads it again. The provider's minimum
cacheable length still applies to the system prompt. Any other value is
treated as `'default'`.
`TokenUsage` reports
`cacheReadInputTokens` / `cacheCreationInputTokens`, plus
`cacheCreationEphemeral5mInputTokens` / `cacheCreationEphemeral1hInputTokens`
when the provider returns the split; `book.costOf` prices each at its own rate.

The `direction` field carries the model-class semantic (`reasoning` /
`drafting` / `extraction`) so per-conversation / per-project rollups can break
down "spent X on reasoning + Y on extraction" natively.

For auditing, `setModelSpanSink(sink)` (core export) registers an optional
process-wide sink that receives a `ModelSpan` — the call's `TokenUsage` plus the
emitting `scope`, e.g. `samba.chatWithToolLoop` — once per underlying model call,
from **every** adapter and every entry point (`chat`, `chatWithTools`, and
`chatWithToolLoop`). A `chatWithToolLoop` call emits one span per iteration with
that iteration's own usage, so expect multiple spans from a single loop call.
Off by default; fail-soft; pass `null` to detach.

## Advisor pair

`withAdvisor(tools, executor, advisor)` (core export, SDK-free) wraps a tool
set + executor so a cheap executor model can consult a stronger advisor
mid-loop: it appends a `consult_advisor` ToolDef (question required, context
optional; input never mutated, name collision throws at wrap time) and routes
consult calls to the injected `advisor.chat` — any adapter's `chat`, bound by
the caller — with the advisor's `systemPrompt` and `modelClass: 'reasoning'`.
The advisor guides, it never certifies: its reply returns as an ordinary tool
result. A failing advisor yields a legible "advisor unavailable" result rather
than a throw, so a dead advisor never kills the work; a missing or empty
question returns a legible ask-again result without calling the advisor.
Optional `onConsult`
hook (fail-soft, not fired on advisor failure) reports each consult's
question/context/answer/usage for consult-rate metrics; the advisor's own
adapter emits its model span as usual.

## Model catalog + provider routing

Model identity is de-brittled — decisions key on `provider/family`, not the exact
version string, so a version bump doesn't zero a model's cost.

- `registerModelCatalog(entries)` / `ModelCatalogEntry` — an adapter declares each
  family once; `models` / `rates` / labels derive from it. `normalizeModelId(id)`
  resolves a drifted version forward to `{ provider, family }`; `catalogEntryFor`,
  `modelLabel`, `registerModelLabels` round it out.
- Provider connection registry — adapters register their connection on import, so
  routing can answer `isProviderConfigured` / `configuredProviders`,
  `providersForFamily(family)` (the inverse index), and `resolveModel({ family?, modelClass?, configuredOnly?, prefer? })`
  (cheapest configured by default). `resolveModelByTerm(term, opts)` resolves a
  loose human term ("deepseek") to a catalog entry; `modelConnection(term, opts)`
  returns a ready OpenAI-compatible `{ provider, modelId, baseUrl, apiKey }`.
  A connection may also declare `altKeyEnvs` — additional env vars whose presence makes
  the provider usable, because the credential CHECK must recognise every credential the
  CALL path accepts. Anthropic declares `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`, so the subscription
  token alone configures it, with no `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` needed.
- `<PROVIDER>_BASE_URL` overrides — every adapter honours an env override for its
  endpoint (`OPENAI_BASE_URL`, `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`, `GEMINI_BASE_URL` /
  `GOOGLE_BASE_URL`, `MISTRAL_BASE_URL`, `DEEPSEEK_BASE_URL`, `SAMBA_NOVA_BASE_URL`),
  so a provider can be pointed at a gateway / proxy / regional / self-hosted
  endpoint without a code change. The override is keyed by **provider/endpoint,
  not model**: running DeepSeek-V3 *via SambaNova* uses `SAMBA_NOVA_*`, not
  `DEEPSEEK_*`. Setting only `OPENAI_BASE_URL` with no key is treated as a
  **keyless local endpoint** (LM Studio / Ollama / vLLM) — the generic OpenAI
  client builds with a placeholder key and routing counts it usable. Every other
  hosted provider (Anthropic, Gemini, SambaNova, Mistral, DeepSeek) always needs
  its key; a base-URL override alone does not make it configured. Routing sees
  only providers whose subpath has been imported.
- `TokenUsage.costUsdReported` (claude-cli only) — the CLI's own `total_cost_usd`: API-equivalent
  on a subscription login, billed money on a metered Console login; the field cannot tell
  which. Absent (never defaulted to 0/NaN; a reported 0 is relayed, a -0 becomes 0) unless a finite number >= 0. A malformed value sets
  `TokenUsage.costUsdReportedInvalidType` (`negative`, `non-finite` or the type name)
  and the span attribute
  `verevoir.llm.cost_usd_reported_invalid_type` instead. Other adapters
  leave it absent (cost comes from the PriceBook).
- Anthropic subscription auth — the Anthropic adapter prefers
  `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` (a Claude subscription token from `claude setup-token`)
  over the metered `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, sending it as a bearer token with the
  required `anthropic-beta` flag + a Claude-Code system identity (both overridable
  via `ANTHROPIC_OAUTH_BETA` / `ANTHROPIC_OAUTH_SYSTEM`). Precedence: an explicit
  per-call `apiKey` → `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` → `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` (fallback
  only), so a set subscription token means the metered key is never billed.

## Status

Pre-stable: the `0.x` line communicates that the API surface can shift before
`1.0`. Track changes in the repo's CHANGELOG.
